title: Last Forever (2)
novel:
Ted [[concluded|conclude]] his story. He told his children, Penny and Luke, about the years that followed Tracy's death. He described how he raised them alone, filled with both [[grief|grief]] and gratitude for the time he had with their mother.

The children sat in silence for a long moment. Then Penny spoke up. She told her father that she understood what he was really doing. This story was not just about how he met their mother. It was about Robin. After all those years, Ted still loved Robin.

Penny told her father that it had been six years since their mother [[passed away|pass away]]. She said that Tracy would have wanted him to be happy. Luke agreed. He told Ted that it was time to [[pursue|pursue]] his feelings for Robin.

Ted was [[shocked|shock]] by his children's [[insight|insight]]. He had tried to hide his feelings, but they had seen through him. He realized that his love for Robin had never truly [[faded|fade]]. It had been there all along, waiting patiently.

With his children's [[blessing|blessing]], Ted went to Robin's apartment. He stood outside her window, holding a blue French horn. It was a [[callback|callback]] to their first date, many years ago. Robin saw him from her window and smiled.

The story came full [[circle|circle]]. Ted had spent years searching for the perfect woman, only to find her and lose her. And now, after everything, he was returning to where his [[journey|journey]] began. The blue horn was a symbol of [[enduring|endure]] love.

Ted and Robin stood together, older and wiser. They had both experienced love, loss, and [[heartbreak|heartbreak]]. But in each other, they found something that had lasted a [[lifetime|lifetime]]. As the screen faded to black, the audience knew that some love stories never truly end. They just find their way back to where they [[belonged|belong]].

callback.en: It was a callback to the first episode.
